title: Shieldfreeden
text: The next day. The process of hatching the Filolial-samas is proceeding smoothly.
“Now, Yuki-chan and Kou will carry the newly hatched Filolial-samas on their backs to help them level up and feed them.”
“Got it!”
“Roger!”
“‘Piyo piyo!’”

After saluting, Yuki-chan and the others ran off, carrying the Filolial-samas of various colors on their backs. So far, we’ve hatched one-third of the total. As long as there’s at least one Filo-tan among them—even if it’s just by color—we can’t… interrupt their training. We simply cannot stop the Filolial hatching process halfway through.
“Whoa… Motoyasu-kun. This has gotten pretty wild, hasn’t it?”
My Father came to visit me in the room I’d been assigned. The room is absolutely packed with the Filolial-sama chicks. They’re all chirping away energetically.
“There’ll be even more by tomorrow.”
“Umm… aren’t you collecting too many?”
“What are you talking about? We’re going to raise even more.”
“There are so many. Sakura’s starting to have fun, too.”
“It looks like we’re on our way to forming a Filolial Army… I wonder how we’ll handle food costs?”
“The Filolial-samas will procure their own supplies.”
“…I’m scared the nearby monsters might get wiped out.”
What on earth is my Father saying? The number of monsters is decreasing, and the number of Filolial-samas is increasing. A paradise will be created.
Besides, this many isn’t a problem yet. With that in mind, I continued hatching the Filolial-sama… but there wasn’t a single one with the color scheme that matched Filo-tan!
“Oh no…”

I put both hands on the ground and groaned. How could this be? I bought up every single Filolial-sama from the monster merchant, yet I still can’t find Filo-tan. Was Father’s story about buying them from that monster merchant a mistake after all?
What should I do? At this rate, Filo-tan will end up being bought by some random stranger I don’t even know. What should I do!
There’s a limit to how much money I can get from Siltvelt. I’ll have to come up with a new plan.
“Alright, let’s take turns leveling up!”

Yuki-chan and the others, who finished their Class Up long ago, are steadily leveling up Filolial-sama. With their spear skills and enhanced latent abilities, there’s no monster that can stand up to them—at least not easily. But first, we need to make some plans.
Ah, Filo-tan, where are you, my beloved? My heart is screaming that I, Motoyasu, want to fly right to you. I suppose we should go hunt bandits first.
“So, we’ll hunt bandits to raise money while searching for the Hero of the Claw.”
“Understood.”
“Hey, do bandits taste good?”
“Motoyasu-kun, please prioritize the search for the Hero of the Claw. Also, Kou, please don’t learn how to eat people.”
“Hmm…”

Sakura-chan is dozing off while riding on her Father’s back. I gently gaze at her sleeping face. Oh? Is it just my imagination? I feel like I caught a scent from Sakura-chan that’s very similar to Filo-tan’s. Well, I suppose it’s just my imagination.
“Well then, I’m off!”
“Have a good trip. I’ll be heading out with Sakura-chan in a little while, too.”

And so, daily life in Siltvelt went on. My father later told me that, starting that day, he’d been riding around on Sakura-chan to explore various parts of Siltvelt. It felt like the first time I’d ever seen him like this.

He shared stories of battles in another world, real combat experience—adventures that went far beyond just riding around on Sakura-chan. The people of Siltvelt were also very supportive of my Father, and his popularity was skyrocketing as he dealt earnestly with incidents.
And so, that seemingly peaceful daily life passed… and the Siltvelt Wave was now just three days away…
“The Wave, huh… I know it’s probably inappropriate to say, but I’m actually looking forward to it a little.”
“My heart was racing, too, when I faced the Wave for the first time.”

I still remember it clearly. I remember relying on my gaming knowledge to unleash Skills against the chimera that appeared in the Wave. I recall it being a very enjoyable battle. However, my Father looked quite displeased.

After that, with talk of my Big Sister being worked to the bone as a slave by the Crimson Swine—and that we absolutely had to rescue her—I challenged him to a duel without realizing that my Father and my Big Sister were in cahoots. That was the biggest blunder of my life, Motoyasu. What’s more, my Father racked his brains and accomplished the remarkable feat of forcing me, Motoyasu, to the ground.

It was a fighting style unique to my Father, who had extensive experience in PvP. Yet I couldn’t admit defeat; instead of surrendering, I kept trying to figure out a way to turn the tables. How foolish of me to challenge my Father to a duel when I had no way to attack him. But Father used a monster to wound me. That alone settled the match.
I lost. I must learn that kind of defiant spirit from Father. Even if I have to swallow muddy water, I’ll make sure to meet Filo-tan.
I’ve saved up a little money from hunting bandits. Now, which monster merchant in Melromarc should I buy from next?
Such peaceful days continued. Then, the very next day.
“Dispatch the Seven Star Heroes who oversee Shieldfreeden and Faubrey?”
At the morning meeting, the representative of the Shusaku clan reported this to my Father and me.
“Huh? But isn’t it okay since Motoyasu and I are in Siltvelt?”

“That’s true, but given that… the Hero of the Claw—who is supposed to protect our country and our neighbors—is currently missing, it’s been decided that each nation will send representatives as a precaution.”
“Huh…”
“I did say that our country could handle the waves just by having the Shield Hero here…”
“Well, I guess it’s just better safe than sorry?”
My Father nodded repeatedly. Then he motioned for me to come closer, as if to whisper something in my ear.
“To be honest… Siltvelt is a surprisingly extreme country, isn’t it? I get special treatment because I’m a Hero, but when I see humans being treated like slaves…”
“That’s true.”

Admittedly, I, Motoyasu, don’t recall having been to any places other than Melromarc and a few other countries, but I do get the impression that humans aren’t treated very well. Even when we hunt bandits, the vast majority are Demi-Human bandits. Well, I suppose that’s to be expected since it’s a Demi-Human nation.
“How should I put it… something like what would be considered a Viking nation by my world’s standards? Or perhaps like the United Kingdom, where bloodlines are highly valued?”
“Is that so?”
“Yeah. I hear bloodline is taken very seriously in this country.”

My Father told me what he’d learned in Siltvelt. Siltvelt is a country founded on the worship of the Shield Hero, and its upper echelons are apparently held by famous lineages that have continued for generations. In other words, noble status is inherited through bloodline.

My father explained that it’s much the same everywhere in this world. Among them, the four races at the very top—Shusaku, Genmu, Aotatsu, and Hakuko—are said to resemble the Four Sacred Beasts, which are famous even in our world. However, Hakuko was weakened politically after being held responsible for a great war in the past, and now holds the lowest position among the four top-tier races.

Even among the Demi-Humans of Siltvelt, these four races possess high combat prowess, and thanks to their track record of responding swiftly to Siltvelt’s waves and minimizing damage, they reportedly still enjoy domestic support to this day.
“So, apparently, the people who couldn’t keep up with that bloodline-centric policy went on to found a country called Shieldfreeden.”

Shieldfreeden. This country’s history is said to be very short compared to Siltvelt’s. It’s a newcomer nation, having been established only about a hundred years ago… a country born, so to speak, at the very edge of the frontier spirit.
“According to what I heard from someone from that country, it was founded by races of ‘lowly’ lineage who left the country because they couldn’t follow our nation’s traditional policies…”
“I don’t really get it.”

“Well… why not just think of it as a country formed by low-wage workers who made up their minds to emigrate? It’s probably not as extreme as Melromarc, which seems to be a human-supremacist nation, but since there are various Demi-Human races, there’s bound to be some bloodline discrimination, and I imagine there’s always been a bit of discrimination since way back.”
There are countries in our world with similar histories, aren’t there? I guess that means the world is pretty much the same everywhere.
“I see… There’s a country with a similar history in the world I came from, too.”

“Yeah. Apparently, that’s how that country was founded. That’s why they had something called the ‘Slave War’ there a long time ago between humans and Demi-Humans—even though, on the surface, it’s supposedly a country without discrimination.”
“‘On the surface’—you sure do use some unusual turns of phrase, Father.”

“Well… it’s hard to say if it’s really true… It’s just my own impression, though. But since, one way or another, it seems undeniable that Demi-Humans are in charge of the country, I might not be wrong after all.”
“Did you want to go to Shieldfreeden?”
My father began to ponder my question. If there’s a next time, depending on the circumstances, going to Shieldfreeden might be one option. Of course, only if my father wants to, though.

“Hmm… Well, if anything, I’m talking about what would happen if we ended up looping again. For that reason, don’t you think it would be better for Motoyasu-kun to know what kind of country Shieldfreeden is?”
I see. Father’s point is well taken. If I don’t know what kind of country it is, I’ll end up failing if we do end up looping again.

If Father were the one looping, I wouldn’t have to worry, but unfortunately, it’s me who’s looping. If I—the one stuck in the loop—don’t memorize the state of the world and such, I might end up making the same kind of mistakes. I suppose that’s what my Father is worried about.
“So, apparently, the race known as the Aotatsu—which ranks among the highest in Siltvelt—has infiltrated the upper echelons, or rather, the governing body, of this country called Shieldfreeden.”
“The Aotatsu?”
The Aotatsu, huh? I feel like I’ve seen them somewhere before, but I can’t quite place it.

“Right. They’re not exactly nonexistent in Siltvelt, but apparently, just like the Hakuko race, they hold relatively little power. I hear the Hakuko race drove them out in the past, but I haven’t been able to dig up the details yet.”

So, in effect, Siltvelt is run by the Shusaku and Genmu races—those of Demi-Human descent. Hmm? Come to think of it… I seem to recall hearing from someone that these two races are, if anything, on the moderate side. Well, it wouldn’t be surprising if radical factions were rising even within those groups. Father stops whispering and responds with a smile to the Shusaku representative.
“So, when are those Seven Star Heroes expected to arrive?”
“They’re scheduled to have an audience tomorrow at noon.”
“I see… Got it. I’ll make sure to be at the castle by then.”
“We’re truly grateful.”
And with that, the meeting came to a close.
